issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement (Part 3) explicitly requires Farm to aggregate animals using a List implemented as an ArrayList and to initialize that ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. The solution implementation declares the field as private Set<Animal> animals, initializes it as a new HashSet<>(), and exposes getter/setter with type Set<Animal>. The template contains a TODO placeholder for Farm but does not provide a concrete field. This mismatch causes confusion about the expected collection type and the signatures of the getter/setter (List<Animal> vs Set<Animal>), and about ordering/duplicate semantics students must support.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: change the solution to use List<Animal> animals (import java.util.List) and initialize it in the no-arg constructor as new ArrayList<>(); update the getter and setter signatures to return/accept List<Animal>. If Set semantics were intended instead, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a Set/HashSet and explain the difference so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: Concept: the Farm's collection of Animal instances. In the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 108-111) the collection is specified as a List and explicitly instructs to initialize an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) contains a TODO to implement the Farm collection but no concrete collection type. The solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) defines the field as private Set<Animal> animals and instantiates it with new HashSet<>() (losing the List/ArrayList wording). Students reading the task will expect List/ArrayList semantics (ordering, indexing, List API) and signatures (getter/setter using List<Animal>), but the solution uses Set/HashSet which has different semantics (no ordering, no duplicates) and different type in the field/getter/setter. This naming/type mismatch between the described collection (ArrayList/List) and the implemented collection (HashSet/Set) can confuse students about which collection type they must use and which behaviors the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to use the List interface and ArrayList implementation (declare private List<Animal> animals; instantiate with new ArrayList<>(); and update getter/setter to return/accept List<Animal>) so it matches the problem statement; or (B) Update the problem statement and template to accept a Set-based implementation (replace 'List'/'ArrayList' wording with 'Set'/'HashSet') and clarify the intended semantics (ordering/duplicates). Option A is recommended to preserve the current exercise wording.
